question: What term describes the complete absence of all microorganisms from an object or area?
explanation: Surgical asepsis, or sterile technique, destroys and eliminates all forms of microbial life, including spores. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h1)

question: What is the main difference between medical asepsis and surgical asepsis?

options.A: Medical asepsis reduces germ numbers while surgical asepsis removes all microorganisms.
options.B: Medical asepsis is only for operating rooms while surgical asepsis is for wards.
options.C: Medical asepsis uses autoclaves while surgical asepsis uses chemical sprays.
options.D: Medical asepsis prevents blood infections while surgical asepsis prevents airborne ones.

explanation: Medical asepsis focuses on clean technique to lower pathogen counts, whereas surgical asepsis demands complete sterility. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h1)

question: Which area of the surgical suite allows personnel to wear regular street clothes?
explanation: The unrestricted zone serves as the entrance for patients and staff where street clothes are still allowed. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h2)

question: A nurse enters a storage room containing wrapped sterile instrument trays. What clothing is required?

options.C: Street clothes with a lab coat

explanation: Instrument storage areas are semi-restricted zones requiring dedicated scrub suits and caps to limit particle shedding. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h2)

question: Why must scrubbed hands be held higher than the elbows during a surgical scrub?

options.A: To prevent water from running down from the unwashed arms to the hands
options.B: To keep the arm pulse elevated and reduce blood flow to the fingers
options.C: To allow air drying of the fingertips before putting on sterile gloves
options.D: To make it easier to slip into the sterile gown sleeves without help

explanation: Gravity ensures water flows from the cleanest area (hands) to the less clean area (elbows), preventing backflow contamination. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h3)

question: A nurse finishes scrubbing and accidentally touches an unsterile tap with the elbow. What should be done?

options.A: Repeat the entire surgical hand scrub from the beginning
options.B: Proceed to gowning since elbows are outside the sterile field
options.C: Rinse only the contaminated elbow thoroughly with sterile saline
options.D: Wipe the affected elbow with alcohol-soaked cotton

explanation: Any break in technique compromises sterility, requiring a full repeat scrub to ensure patient safety. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h3)

question: Which part of a surgical gown worn by the scrub nurse is considered sterile?

options.A: The entire front and back surface from shoulders to floor
options.B: Only the fingertips and the palms of the sterile gloves
options.C: The collar down to the waist including the back panels
options.D: Chest down to the sterile field and sleeves from above the elbow to cuffs

explanation: Gown sterility is strictly limited to the front torso (chest to table level) and sleeves from two inches above the elbow to the cuffs. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h4)

question: Why does a damp sterile drape ruin the safety of a sterile field?

options.A: Wet drapes reflect overhead operating lights and blind the assistants
options.B: Water destroys the sterilizing chemicals inside the woven fabric
options.C: Moisture lets bacteria pass through the barrier from unsterile surfaces
options.D: Moisture pulls dust particles directly into the surgical wound

explanation: Capillary action draws moisture and microbes through porous damp materials, contaminating the sterile zone below. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h4)

question: When is the best time to give antibiotics before a surgical cut is made?

options.B: Only if the patient develops a fever

explanation: Administering antibiotics within one hour prior to incision ensures adequate drug concentration in the tissue when contamination might occur. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h5)

question: Why is it important to keep normal body temperature during surgery?

options.A: It keeps the surgical team comfortable in the theatre.
options.B: It protects immune function and lowers the risk of wound infections.
options.C: It speeds up how fast anesthetic drugs work.
options.D: It ensures accurate blood pressure readings.

explanation: Perioperative hypothermia causes blood vessel constriction and impairs white blood cell function, directly increasing infection risk. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h5)

question: What is the main duty of the circulating nurse regarding sterile technique?

options.A: Giving intravenous anesthetic drugs during the operation
options.B: Monitoring and enforcing sterile boundaries throughout the procedure
options.C: Suturing the skin layers at the end of the surgery
options.D: Performing the initial hand scrub and draping the patient

explanation: The unscrubbed circulating nurse observes the room, tracks potential contamination, and protects the sterile field. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h6)

question: Why must the circulating nurse have the power to stop surgery if there is a sterile break?

options.A: Surgeons are not allowed to touch contaminated instruments.
options.B: Immediate action stops the patient from being exposed to germs.
options.C: Scrub nurses lack the training to spot dirty instruments.
options.D: Hospital rules require a signed incident form before surgery continues.

explanation: Stopping a breach instantly protects the patient from developing severe postoperative surgical site infections. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h6)
